newsitem.title: CHINA: China to allow asset appraisal joint ventures.
newsitem.headline: China to allow asset appraisal joint ventures.

text.p: China will allow foreign firms to set up joint ventures for asset appraisal, the official China Securities said on Tuesday.

But foreign firms will be barred from setting up wholly owned asset appraisal operations in China, the newspaper said, quoting new rules issued by the National Administration of State Property and the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation.
Foreign companies will be allowed to open only one such joint venture, which must have registered capital of at least $500,000. The life of the venture would not exceed 30 years, the newspaper said.

The business scope of such joint ventures could include the evaluation of liquid assets, long-term investments, property, machinery and equipment, construction projects and intangible assets, according to the regulations.
The creation of asset appraisal joint ventures must be approved by the Chinese government and their operations will be supervised by the National Administration of State Property.
Beijing has said the loss of state assets costs China huge sums of money every year, and has sought to boost the ability to asess state property.
